title: K-projective identity denominators are initial with essential value
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$ and derived localization $Q_h:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P$ be a K-projective complex: every chain map from $P$ to a complex with zero cohomology in every degree is chain homotopic to zero, where a chain homotopy has the formula $f-g=d h+h d$. Let $S/P$ be the cofiltered category whose objects are quasi-isomorphisms $s:Y\to P$ in $K(\mathcal A)$, and whose arrows $s\to s'$ are maps $u:Y\to Y'$ with $s'u=s$ [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Then $1_P$ is an initial object of $S/P$. More explicitly, for every $s$ there is a unique $t_s:P\to Y$ with $s t_s=1_P$; it satisfies $Q_h(t_s)=Q_h(s)^{-1}$ and $u t_s=t_{s'}$ for every arrow $u:s\to s'$. For any category $\mathcal H$ and any functor $F:K(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal H$, the denominator diagram $G:S/P\to\mathcal H$, $G(s:Y\to P)=F(Y)$, is essentially constant with value $F(P)$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. It has a witnessing cone $u_s=F(t_s)$ whose leg at $1_P$ is $1_{F(P)}$, a retraction $r=1_{F(P)}$ at stage $1_P$, and common stage $1_P$ for every denominator in the factorization criterion of that definition.

proof.text: For a denominator $s:Y\to P$, localization makes $Q_h(s)$ invertible. Apply the Hom bijection to the K-projective source $P$ and target $Y$: there is a unique $t_s:P\to Y$ with $Q_h(t_s)=Q_h(s)^{-1}$. Functoriality gives $Q_h(s t_s)=1_{Q_hP}=Q_h(1_P)$; injectivity of the same bijection with target $P$ gives $s t_s=1_P$. Conversely, any section $v$ has $Q_h(v)=Q_h(s)^{-1}$ by cancellation of the invertible $Q_h(s)$, hence $v=t_s$ by injectivity with target $Y$. Only $P$, not $Y$, needs to be K-projective.

proof.text: By the definition of arrows in $S/P$, a morphism $1_P\to s$ is precisely a section of $s$. Step 1 therefore proves initiality. For an arrow $u:s\to s\prime$, the relation $s\prime u=s$ gives $s\prime(u t_s)=s t_s=1_P$, so uniqueness gives $u t_s=t_{s\prime}$. Also $t_{1_P}=1_P$. For completeness, this initial object itself witnesses cofilteredness: it gives a nonempty category and a common source for every pair of objects; for parallel arrows $a,b:s\to s\prime$, both $a t_s$ and $b t_s$ equal $t_{s\prime}$, so precomposition with $t_s:1_P\to s$ equalizes them.

source.place: Tags 05S8 and 05S9, situation-derived-functor and definition-right-derived-functor-defined; agent-written K-projective denominator argument using the Hom bijection stated in lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection.

proof.text: Fix any functor $F$ as in the statement and set $u_s=F(t_s):F(P)\to F(Y)$. Functoriality and Step 2 give $F(u)u_s=F(u t_s)=F(t_{s\prime})=u_{s\prime}$, so these legs form a cone over $G$. At $j_0=1_P$, its leg is $F(1_P)=1_{F(P)}$. In the pro-diagram criterion take $r=1_{F(P)}$. For each denominator $s$, take $k=1_P$, the arrow $k\to j_0$ to be the identity and $k\to s$ to be $t_s$. The required transition factorization is exactly $G(t_s)=F(t_s)=u_s\,r\,G(1_{1_P})$, and $r u_{j_0}=1_{F(P)}$. Together with the cofilteredness just checked, these are every clause of essential constancy with the asserted value and common stage.
